source_text: Καὶ οἱ μὲν περὶ τὰ εἴδωλα αὐτοὺς ἕλκοντες οἱ δαίμονές εἰσιν οἱ προειρημένοι, οἱ προστετηκότες τῷ ἀπὸ τῶν ἱερείων αἵματι καὶ ταῦτα περιλιχμώμενοι· οἱ δὲ τοῖς πολλοῖς ἀρέσκοντες θεοὶ καὶ ταῖς εἰκόσιν ἐπονομαζόμενοι, ὡς ἔστιν ἐκ τῆς κατ᾿ αὐτοὺς ἱστορίας εἰδέναι, ἄνθρωποι γεγόνασιν. Καὶ τους μὲν δαίμονας εἶναι τοὺς ἐπιβατεύοντας τοῖς ὀνόμασι πίστις ἡ ἑκάστου αὐτῶν ἐνέργεια. Οἱ μὲν γὰρ ἀποτέμνουσι τὰ αἰδοῖα, οἱ περὶ τὴν Ῥέαν, οἱ δὲ ἐγκόπτουσιν ἢ ἐντέμνουσιν, οἱ περὶ τὴν Ἄρτεμιν, καὶ ἡ μὲν ἐν Ταύροις φονεύει τοὺς ξένους· ἐῶ γὰρ τοὺς ταῖς μαχαίραις καὶ τοῖς ἀστραγάλοις αἰκιζομένους αὐτοὺς λέγειν καὶ ὅσα εἴδη δαιμόνων· οὐ γὰρ θεοῦ κινεῖν ἐπὶ τὰ παρὰ φύσιν. Ὅταν δ᾿ ὁ δαίμων ἀνδρὶ πορσύνῃ κακά, Τὸν νοῦν ἔβλαψε πρῶτον. Ὁ δὲ θεός, τελείως ἀγαθὸς ὤν, ἀϊδίως ἀγαθοποιός ἐστιν. Τοῦ τοίνυν ἄλλους μὲν εἶναι τοὺς ἐνεργοῦντας, ἐφ᾿ ἑτέρων δὲ ἀνίστασθαι τὰς εἰκόνας, ἐκεῖνο μέγιστον τεκμήριον, Τρωὰς καὶ Πάριον· ἡ μὲν Νερυλλίνου εἰκόνας ἔχει, ὃς ἀνὴρ τῶν καθ᾿ ἡμᾶς, τὸ δὲ Πάριον Ἀλεξάνδρου καὶ Πρωτέως· τοῦ Ἀλεξάνδρου ἔτι ἐπὶ τῆς ἀγορᾶς καὶ ὁ τάφος καὶ ἡ εἰκών.Οἱ μὲν οὖν ἄλλοι ἀνδριάντες τοῦ Νερυλλίνου κόσμημά εἰσι δημόσιον, εἴπερ καὶ τούτοις κοσμεῖται πόλις, εἷς δὲ αὐτῶν καὶ χρηματίζειν καὶ ἰᾶσθαι νοσοῦντας νομίζεται, καὶ θύουσί τε δι᾿ αὐτὰ καὶ χρυσῷ περιαλείφουσι καὶ στεφανοῦσι τὸν ἀνδριάντα οἱ Τρωαδεῖς. Ὁ δὲ τοῦ Ἀλεξάνδρου καὶ ὁ τοῦ Πρωτέως (τοῦτον δ᾿ οὐκ ἀγνοεῖτε ῥίψαντα ἑαυτὸν εἰς τὸ πῦρ περὶ τὴν Ὀλυμπίαν), ὁ μὲν καὶ αὐτὸς λέγεται χρηματίζειν, τῷ δὲ τοῦ Ἀλεξάνδρου [Δύσπαρι, εἶδος ἄριστε, γυναιμανές] δημοτελεῖς ἄγονται θυσίαι καὶ ἑορταὶ ὡς ἐπηκόῳ θεῷ. Πότερον οὖν ὁ Νερυλλῖνος καὶ ὁ Πρωτεὺς καὶ ὁ Ἀλέξανδρός εἰσιν οἱ ταῦτα ἐνεργοῦντες περὶ τὰ ἀγάλματα ἢ τῆς ὕλης ἡ σύστασις; Ἀλλ᾿ ἡ μὲν ὕλη χαλκός ἐστιν. Τί δαὶ χαλκὸς δύναται καθ᾿ ἑαυτόν, ὃν μεταποιῆσαι πάλιν εἰς ἕτερον σχῆμα ἔξεστιν, ὡς τὸν ποδονιπτῆρα ὁ παρὰ τῷ Ἡροδότῳ Ἄμασις; Ὁ δὲ Νερυλλῖνος καὶ ὁ Πρωτεὺς καὶ ὁ Ἀλέξανδρος τί πλέον τοῖς νοσοῦσιν; Ἃ γὰρ ἡ εἰκὼν λέγεται νῦν ἐνεργεῖν, ἐνήργει καὶ ζῶντος καὶ νοσοῦντος Νερυλλίνου.
pass_a_gloss: And the ones concerning the idols, they are the demons who are drawing them, the ones who have been mentioned before, who have been appointed over the blood from the sacrifices and these are being licked around; and the ones who are pleasing to the many and are being named gods and images, as it is to know from the history concerning them, have become men. And the faith of each of them is the energy by which the demons are treading upon the names. For some are cutting off the genitals, those concerning Rhea, and some are striking or cutting, those concerning Artemis, and the one in Tauris is killing the strangers; for I allow those who are being mistreated by the swords and the dice to speak and the kinds of demons; for it is not the nature of God to move towards the things contrary to nature. When the demon is bringing evils to a man, he first harms the mind. But God, being completely good, is always doing good. Therefore, the fact that there are others who are acting and others upon whom the images are being set up, this is the greatest proof, Troy and Parius; the one has images of Neryllinus, who is a man among us, and the other has images of Alexander and Proteus; and the tomb and image of Alexander are still in the marketplace. The other statues of Neryllinus are a public ornament, if indeed the city is also being ornamented by these, and one of them is even thought to prophesy and heal the sick, and the Trojans are sacrificing and anointing with gold and crowning the statue. And the one of Alexander and the one of Proteus (this one, you are not unaware, threw himself into the fire concerning the Olympic games), the one is also said to prophesy, and to the one of Alexander, public sacrifices and festivals are being held as to an attendant god. Are then Neryllinus and Proteus and Alexander the ones who are acting concerning these statues or is it the composition of the material? But the material is bronze. What then can bronze do by itself, which can be remade again into another shape, like the foot-basin which Amasis, the one by Herodotus, made? And what more can Neryllinus and Proteus and Alexander do for the sick? For what the image is said to be doing now, Neryllinus was also doing while he was alive and sick.

choices.why: faith is the energy of the demons treading the names

pass_b_english: The demons I mentioned earlier are the ones who drag people toward idols, appointed over the blood of sacrifices and licking it up. The figures whom the masses call gods and honor with images, as their own histories show, were merely human beings. It is each person's faith that supplies the energy by which demons trample the names. Some castrate themselves, the devotees of Rhea; others flagellate or cut themselves, the devotees of Artemis; the priestess in Tauris kills strangers — I let those abused by swords and dice, and the various kinds of demons, speak for themselves — for it is not in the nature of God to drive anyone toward what is contrary to nature. When a demon brings evils upon a man, it first damages his mind. But God, being perfectly good, is eternally doing good. Therefore, the fact that some men act while images are erected to others stands as the greatest proof: Troy and Parium. Troy has images of Neryllinus, a man of our own time; Parium has images of Alexander and Proteus, and Alexander's tomb and image still stand in the marketplace. The other statues of Neryllinus serve as public ornaments, if a city can be adorned by such things, and one of them is even believed to prophesy and heal the sick; the Trojans sacrifice because of it, anoint the statue with gold, and crown it. The statue of Alexander and that of Proteus — you know he threw himself into the fire at Olympia — the former is also said to prophesy, and public sacrifices and festivals are held for Alexander's statue as for an attendant god. Are Neryllinus, Proteus, and Alexander the ones acting through these statues, or is it the material itself? But the material is bronze. What can bronze do by itself, when it can be melted down and reshaped into another form, like the foot-basin King Amasis made, as Herodotus tells? And what more can Neryllinus, Proteus, and Alexander do for the sick? Whatever the image is said to do now, Neryllinus was already doing while he was alive and sick.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Greek text. Pass A provides a literal rendering, while Pass B provides a more fluent English version that maintains the theological and historical nuances. All clauses, including the specific examples of Rhea, Artemis, and the Tauris priestess, are accounted for. The distinction between the nature of God and the actions of demons is preserved. The reference to Amasis and Herodotus is correctly handled. The bracketed Greek text [Δύσπαρι, εἶδος ἄριστε, γυναιμανές] is treated as an interpolation/uncertainty and is not misrepresented in the English.
